contents.name: Sections 29.1.1-29.1.3, desiderata: the canonical sheaf of a projective k-scheme, vector-bundle duality, and duality for general X and F

Proposition 29.1.8, uniqueness of the canonical sheaf and trace

Sections 29.1.12-29.1.13, the Ext form of duality and its trace version
Section 29.1.14, necessity of the Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis
contents.reason: The remark records that the vector-bundle form needs Cohen-Macaulay hypotheses; the pair proves only the positive CM theorem and states no necessity counterexample, so no item carries this remark.

contents.name: Section 29.2.2, functorial Serre duality for Ext on projective space

Section 29.2.4 and Exercises 29.2.L-29.2.M: local-to-global Ext spectral sequence
contents.reason: The selected coherent-duality theorem is established by finite ambient twisted locally free resolutions and derived evaluation. Neither its statement nor a supplier needs the spectral sequence Hi(X, sheaf Ext^j) => Ext^(i+j); the locally free comparison is retained separately.

contents.name: Sections 29.3.1-29.3.3 and Exercises 29.4.A-29.4.B, the functor pi^! and its finite-flat behaviour
Sections 29.3.4-29.3.5, projective schemes as finite covers of projective space and finite projections
contents.reason: The pair constructs the normalized dualizing complex directly from a closed projective embedding and never uses the finite-cover pi^! route, so no item on the pair states those finite-cover results.

contents.name: Sections 29.3.8-29.3.9 and 29.3.11-29.3.12: finite-map transport of vector-bundle/Hom duality and non-CM canonical-sheaf Hom duality
contents.reason: The finite-flat transport proof and the broader non-CM canonical-sheaf Hom theorem are not commissioned claims. The local closed-immersion derived coinduction and normalized dualizing-complex proof supply the selected projective pure-CM coherent result; Corollary29.3.10 remains separately included.

contents.reason: The pair proves coherent duality with a potentially noninvertible dualizing sheaf. A general Gorenstein classification/slicing criterion is not a commissioned result and is not needed by the nodal hypersurface calculation or the retained smooth canonical-bundle comparison.

contents.name: Exercise 29.4.K and Remark 29.4.10: smooth canonical sheaf equals top differential bundle and recovers classical Serre duality
